subject: Re: Immediate: Brightline embeddings p95/p99 spike after catalog promotion
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: support@brightline.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Hi Avery,

We started seeing a large latency regression on the embeddings endpoint right after your model catalog promotion between 08:55 and 09:05 PDT. Our search relevance pipeline (BrightSearch) is timing out — p95 has jumped from ~120ms to ~740ms and p99 is up around 2.8s. This started shortly after we received the new model version ID in the catalog (model:v3.2-optim).

Attached is a small sample (brightline_samples.csv) showing request IDs, timestamps, and latencies. We are blocking on this — users are getting degraded search results and retries are amplifying load. Can you triage ASAP and advise whether you can route our traffic to the previous model variant?

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Product — Brightline AI
[Attachment: brightline_samples.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Elena — thanks for the quick signal and sample. I’m escalating to engineering and CS now.

Quick plan:
- Dev will triage correlation with the catalog promotion and confirm whether the promoted variant changed kernel selection or quantization params.
- If we can confirm a regression, we’ll route Brightline traffic to the previous catalog entry (v3.1) as a mitigation while we investigate.
- We’ll aim to have an initial mitigation or update within 60–90 minutes.

I’ve looped in Dev (Dev Patel) and Rishi to help with rollback options. Laura/Vanessa, feel free to chime in on any commercial remedies (credits/exec briefing).

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Thanks — I'm looking at traces now (pulling logs for the request IDs in the CSV). Early signs point at a change in kernel path selection after promotion of model:v3.2-optim; the planner selected a different attention kernel that appears to create a CPU-side serialization when batch sizes fall below expected thresholds.

Questions for Brightline: can you confirm the request payload sizes and concurrency pattern for the sample requests (the CSV has IDs but not concurrency)? Also, do you have a specific request_id we should prioritize?

Mitigation options I can take immediately:
- Route Brightline traffic to model:v3.1-stable (previous variant) — quick rollback at the catalog/routing layer.
- Force the runtime to use fallback kernel via a runtime flag for only Brightline’s route (less invasive than full rollback).

If you can send one or two request_ids, I’ll pull full traces and confirm which mitigation is faster.

—Dev
Sr. Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Dev — thanks. Two request IDs: bline-req-20280809-0918 and bline-req-20280809-0923 are representative. Concurrency pattern: short bursts from our frontends, typically 1–4 concurrent requests per worker; payloads are standard 768-d vectors, 1 prompt per request.

We measured baseline (pre-promotion) p95 ~120ms / p99 ~340ms. After promotion those move to p95~740ms / p99~2.8s. Searches are timing out after 2s in our infra which is causing fallback behaviors.

We’ve attached the sample CSV with IDs and timestamps. Please advise immediate next steps.

Thanks — Elena
[Attachment: brightline_samples.csv continued]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Team — this is a high-impact customer with an active expansion contract (BR-4701). Elena is asking for rollback + postmortem and will expect commercial remediation if disruption continues.

Proposed immediate steps from GTM:
- Approve routing Brightline to previous model variant as mitigation.
- Offer 2 weeks of pro-rated credits if user-visible impact persists beyond mitigation window.
- Schedule a 30-minute exec briefing today (Brightline execs are standing by).

Marcus/Rishi — can engineering confirm rollback ETA and whether rollback risks other customers?

—Laura
Account Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in embedding latency after catalog push

Acknowledged. We will perform a targeted rollback for Brightline traffic only — staged routing change to point their route at model:v3.1-stable. SRE/Runtime will monitor for side-effects.

Rishi/Dev: please execute the rollback and report back with:
- confirmation when traffic is routed (timestamp)
- p95/p99 observed immediately after routing change
- whether any knobs need to be tweaked to stabilize kernel selection for smaller batches

Also notify Legal/Finance about potential credit decision; Laura can scope.

—Marcus
VP, Product Operations

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, avery_johnson@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: execution: rollback for Brightline route

Rollback executed at 2028-08-09T12:03:12-07:00 — routed all Brightline API keys to model:v3.1-stable via catalog routing rule br_routes/brightline-roll-0809. Initial metrics: p95 down to ~130ms, p99 ~360ms on sampled traffic after 2 minutes. Traces show the kernel path reverted to the previous planner selections; the serialization disappears under this variant.

I’ve attached the small patch we used to toggle the routing (rollback_patch.diff) and a short snippet of the trace logs we pulled to verify (see incident link).

Next steps: I’ll capture a longer 30m trace window and postmortem notes; engineering will then re-open the model:v3.2-optim promotion with adjusted planning knobs and a canary that specifically tests low-concurrency tails.

[Attachment: rollback_patch.diff (text, 3.4KB)]

—Dev

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@brightline.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-09T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: execution: rollback for Brightline route

Elena — we’ve routed your traffic back to the previous model variant at 12:03 PDT. Early metrics show p95/p99 returning to pre-promotion values. I’m sorry for the disruption.

Next steps on our side:
- Engineering will produce a postmortem and a remediation timeline (ETA: EOD today for draft).
- Laura/Vanessa will follow up on credits/exec briefing.
- We’ll schedule a 30-minute review with Brightline next business day to walk the postmortem and the plan to safely re-promote v3.2.

Would you like the exec briefing today or tomorrow morning?

—Avery
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
